note: Words are in Tesseract emission order — the reading order. Never sort this array. Isis Unveiled (1877) Vol. I, HathiTrust scan of the Cornell copy. The scanned volume is NOT on the shelf: merged from its 19 chunks it is 357 MB, well past MAX_SCAN_BYTES. Rebuild it by concatenating coo1-ark--13960-t6640b80d-1788977050_p*.pdf in filename order with pdf-lib — see ISIS-UNVEILED-1877-scans.md on the shelf, which also carries the leaf-to-folio map and the anchors to check a rebuild against. Why these seven leaves: 91 is footnote-heavy — one note fills half the page, so its note lines outnumber its body lines and the median line size lands on the *footnote* size; it is the leaf that decides bodyTypeSize. 99 is clean body under the digitization stamp. 101 has a running head that fell into the body by one pixel and a footnote typed as a paragraph. 200 carries a mis-segmented box measuring 167% of the body and a 2x5 pixel speck that defeats a text-based speck filter. 300 has three footnotes, one measuring taller than the body because its words carry ascenders. 400 has four footnote lines, two too short to measure reliably. 650 has footnote continuation lines carrying no reference mark. 109 and 126 are the two the volume’s own numbering settles rather than the geometry: 109’s head is 73% of the measure and gives up no folio, and its number reads `5I`; 126’s folio is set `68` on the paper and OCR reads it `63`, which is the one case the rule must report and never change. 155 and 171 carry the printer’s signature mark — a lone `7` on folio 97 and a lone `8` on folio 113, each the first leaf of a gathering in a book gathered in 16s. Every leaf carries the HathiTrust footer. 202 is the leaf whose running head measures as display type: a speck of dirt read as a colon puts the line at 39 pixels against a 27-pixel body, and only the folio it carries says it is furniture.
